The data above is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function  $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z>-0.74).$ Use the table above and do not round your answer.

$P(Z>-0.74)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/12f35be1eac4ea4550df9e6e22f6650bcd9d532943902ad8e6239a6b8c6587f9.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>-0.74).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/9608411f431d6a72af9185ce77b723c7145b1d900559ad9f78d125e92416fbe8.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<0.74).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/49e48de25c1183b24176fbfca868c6d07b8367632ad63c158181e3538222fc3d.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>-0.74)=P(Z<0.74)=Φ(0.74)=0.7704.
$$
